knowledge_point.title: Computing an Integral Using the Sum and Constant Factor Rules

question.:question/worked-solution:
Using the sum and constant factor rules, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{x^{5}+2}{x^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}x &= \int \left(x^{3} + \frac{2}{x^{2}}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x \\ &=\int x^{3}\,\mathrm{d}x+2\int x^{-2}\,\mathrm{d}x \\ &=\left(\frac{x^{4}}{4}\right)+2\left(\frac{x^{-1}}{-1}\right)+C \\ &=\frac{x^{4}}{4}-\frac{2}{x}+C.\end{aligned}
$$
